headline: Iran armed forces chief's five-condition security roadmap + Qatar mediation update'
dek: Major-General Ali Abdollahi, chief of staff of Iran's armed forces, laid out a five-condition roadmap to lasting security: end hostilities on all fronts including Lebanon and Gaza; complete lifting of sanctions; unfreezing of Iranian assets plus war reparations; recognition of Iran's sovereignty…
sources: Al Jazeera, reporting Iran's Tasnim news agency (Abdollahi plan) and Qatar MFA spokesman Majed al-Ansari (Doha weekly briefing, Tuesday)
fault_line: Should Washington meet Tehran's price (sanctions off, blockade ended, Hormuz sovereignty recognised) to reopen the strait, or hold the line on a verifiable no-rebuild nuclear commitment first?

sections.what_happened: Major-General Ali Abdollahi, chief of staff of Iran's armed forces, laid out a five-condition roadmap to lasting security: end hostilities on all fronts including Lebanon and Gaza; complete lifting of sanctions; unfreezing of Iranian assets plus war reparations; recognition of Iran's sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz; and a guarantee against future aggression under a regional security framework. Separately, Qatar's Majed al-Ansari said a Qatari delegation met Iranian officials in Tehran for 3+ hours on Monday and both sides are now studying Qatar's proposal; Ghalibaf said 'the ball is in America's court to prevent war'; Tehran's Hamshahri reported Iran updated its target bank to include US bases and infrastructure in Europe; Deputy FM Gharibabadi said Iran is neither waiting for nor shaping policy around the US midterms.
sections.what_verified: AJ (T2, STATE QA) relaying Tasnim (Iranian state agency) for the plan; Qatar MFA briefing via AJ for the mediation detail. No second independent family for the five-condition list itself.
sections.what_disputed: Rezaei's seven conditions (recorded 1900-02) overlap this list but differ in count and content -- the two roadmaps are distinct statements, not one plan; no US acceptance or response to either list is on record. Hamshahri target-bank claim has no US/Iranian official confirmation.
sections.why_matters: Iran's army chief just published his price for peace -- five conditions, and one of them is Hormuz itself
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (AJ published Tue Nov 3, absent from all earlier Nov 3 scans) -- Iran armed forces chief's five-condition security roadmap + Qatar mediation update

totw_analysis: Our read: Iran's army chief just published his price for peace -- five conditions, and one of them is Hormuz itself The fault line our audience is arguing over: Should Washington meet Tehran's price (sanctions off, blockade ended, Hormuz sovereignty recognised) to reopen the strait, or hold the line on a verifiable no-rebuild nuclear commitment first?
